## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `86ee1dfcc3cf5ce4b33b52a6295007759af23103`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/driver.zod.ts, docs/adr/0067-commit-history-and-rollback-for-ai-authoring.md + packages/metadata-protocol/src/sys-metadata-repository.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts

Read, not reviewed: on main (d683e6f, merge base ba35dfd7; none of the cited code moved between them, only six added lines in protocol.ts elsewhere) `packages/drivers/driver-memory/src/memory-driver.ts` (`beginTransaction`, `commit`, `rollback`, `supports`), `packages/core/src/utils/migration-journal.ts` (`engineCanRollBack`), `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-package-commits.ts` (`revertCommit`, `rollbackToPackageCommit`), `protocol-package-commit-record.ts` (`recordPackageCommit`), `protocol.ts` (the two door docblocks), `packages/drivers/driver-odata/src/odata-driver.ts`, `packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/turso-driver.ts`. Also card #32504 with every comment, and the check-runs on the head.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set: none moves. All four files change only comments or ADR prose. No schema, no `.describe()`, no export, no authorable key, no runtime path. Right.
- Public surface: no symbol, signature or type changes. The changed TSDoc does ship (see ②). The generated-artifact gates on the head agree that nothing generated moves. In `Type Check · source gates` (success), the steps "check:generated ledger", "generated reference docs are in sync with the spec" and "generated skill references are in sync" all pass. So no regenerated artifact is owed. `check:api-surface` (in `Type Check · consumer gates`) was still running at review time. The PR body records it at exit 0 locally.
- Check-runs at review time: 15 success, 13 skipped, 20 still running (Build Core, Lint ×6, Test Core 1–8, Type Check workspace, consumer gates, debt ledger, Live E2E UI). None failed. The running ones are the merge gate. This record does not stand in for them.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` in the PR body are right. No author-writable surface moves.
- `skip-changeset` is wrong. **should-fix.** AGENTS.md (Post-Task Checklist, step 3) says the label "is for a diff that publishes nothing from any released package". os-dev.md L297 gives the test: published means what each package's `files[]` actually ships. By that test:
  - `@objectstack/spec` ships `src/**/*.zod.ts` verbatim, so the edited `driver.zod.ts` is itself a shipped file. `driverSupportsTransactions` is also exported, so its TSDoc lands in `dist` d.ts.
  - `@objectstack/objectql` ships `dist`. `ObjectQL.transaction` is public, so its docblock is in the d.ts.
  - `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` ships `dist`. `SysMetadataEngine` is exported from `src/index.ts`, so its `transaction` docblock is in the d.ts.
  - No package sets `removeComments`.
  - Precedent agrees: the metadata-protocol and objectql CHANGELOGs carry a TSDoc-only `patch` entry that says why in these same words ("land in the shipped dist/*.d.ts … All three packages ship dist in files[]").
  - The os-dev.md fast-track line ("注释,不发布", "comments don't publish") contradicts its own L297 test and AGENTS.md. Escalated in ③.
- Check Changeset on the head is `success`, but only through the label exemption. Its job ran the live label re-read and skipped every other step. So the gate never judged this diff, and its green is not evidence either way.
- Fix: one `patch` changeset for `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/objectql` and `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, carrying `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none`. Then remove `skip-changeset`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev deviation "skip-changeset … if the seat reads that as published, a patch changeset … is the fix": the seat reads it as published. See ②. Escalated to the PM/maintainer: os-dev.md's fast-track entry "注释" (comments) conflicts with AGENTS.md step 3 and with os-dev.md L297. That conflict should be ruled in one place, so the next comment-only package diff does not repeat this.
- Dev deviation "ran at the claim's default model; the in-seat contract review is the owed record": answered. This record is that review, at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER.
- Dev deviation "scope: `withTxn` docblock and the D3 `rollbackToPackageCommit` bullet": accepted. Both carry the same defect class in a file the card already names. The card's own quote for `withTxn` is actually the `SysMetadataEngine.transaction` sentence, so both docblocks had to move together. TL;DR 3 names both doors.
- Dev deviation "HTML signature comment vs os-dev.md": not a contract matter, no finding.
- `open_questions`: empty.
- Out-of-scope "whether the revert doors should become atomic": correctly left open and named in the amendment's "does not decide". It stays with the maintainer, as the ruling says (text follows code; revert is not made atomic here).

### ④ Design judgment

**`docs/adr/0067-commit-history-and-rollback-for-ai-authoring.md`**

- **No ruled sentence deleted: holds.** The diff has four modified lines and no removals. On each of them (status line, TL;DR 3, D3 `revertCommit` bullet, D3 `rollbackToPackageCommit` bullet), the original text survives as an exact prefix, with an italic marker or a new `· **Amended**` entry appended. This is the form the #32480 amendment already uses. Nothing else in the record claims revert atomicity unmarked. TL;DR 4's "atomic + revertible commits" is about D2's apply.
- **Amendment against `revertCommit` on main: holds, sentence by sentence.**
  - It walks the items newest first: `[...items].reverse()`.
  - A created item is soft-removed through `repo.delete`. A modified item is restored through `repo.restoreVersion`, which returns `this.put`.
  - `put` and `delete` each run in `withTxn`. The function opens no transaction of its own (zero hits).
  - The stored-type pre-flight pushes to `failed[]` with `code` and `continue`s. The outer `catch` pushes the client-facing text and code.
  - Registry write-through, storage sync and the projector run after the row write, inside the same `try`. So the "row written, item still in `failed[]`" sentence is right.
  - The commit is built from `reverted.map(…)`. `success` is true only when `failed` is empty and `reverted` is non-empty.
  - The "partly reverted" consequence is the honest one, and it matches the `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation#revertCommit` contract.
- **`rollbackToPackageCommit` marker and amendment bullet: hold.**
  - Each `apply` commit strictly newer than the target gets one `revertCommit`, in `listCommits` order (newest first).
  - A step that throws adds one entry. A returned step's `failed[]` items are folded in one by one.
  - Neither stops the loop. The D3 marker "not one transaction; one `revertCommit` per commit, each step's failures collected" is right.
- **should-fix: "every step that returns has recorded its own revert commit" overclaims. The same applies, more softly, to "the revert commit is recorded from `reverted[]`".** The record write is best effort. `recordPackageCommit` catches every error, including an unprovisioned `sys_metadata_commit`, logs at info or error, and returns `null`. `revertCommit` then omits `revertCommitId` and still returns normally. So a returned step can have recorded nothing, and that revert is then neither on the timeline nor itself revertible. That is D3's own append-only promise, in an amendment whose job is to state what the code does. Fix, in prose only: "every step that returns has attempted its own revert commit; the record is best effort (`recordPackageCommit` returns null, logs, and the answer omits `revertCommitId`, when the commit store is unprovisioned or the write fails)". `protocol.ts`'s `rollbackToPackageCommit` docblock ("records its revert commit") has the same gap. It is outside this diff, so it belongs on a follow-up, not here.
- **nit:** "audit rows written during reverted work still remain" uses "reverted" for transaction rollback. In an ADR about `revertCommit`, that reads as the revert door. Suggest "rolled-back work". Either reading is true, so this does not affect the contract.
- **D2 (#32480) not contradicted: holds.** The new section places the per-item `withTxn` rollback behind "the gate of the" #32480 amendment (`engineCanRollBack`). It says it changes nothing in Decision-2 or the publish door. It fills exactly the gap #32480 left ("makes no statement about Decision-3's revert doors"). The new `withTxn` docblock's "a SQL driver is not by itself a guarantee of rollback" agrees with #32480's scope section. The new docblocks' "the in-memory driver rolls back" agrees with #32480's "The in-memory driver is not on that list".

**`packages/spec/src/data/driver.zod.ts`**: holds. Clause 1 now names a test double and a foreign engine as having no `beginTransaction`. It says the in-memory driver implements `beginTransaction` and `rollback` by snapshotting the whole store and restoring the snapshot. This matches `memory-driver.ts`: `beginTransaction` copies every table array and every record, `rollback` swaps `this.db` back, and `supports = {}`. The copy is shallow per record, not the "deep-clone" its own comment says. That is sufficient, because every write path replaces or splices records and never mutates them in place. `driverSupportsTransactions` answers yes for it. The sentence states mechanism only and claims no isolation.

**`packages/metadata-protocol/src/sys-metadata-repository.ts`** and **`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`**

- **should-fix: the claims around rollback hold, but three sentences drop the caveat that #32480 already records.** The sentences are `SysMetadataEngine.transaction`'s "The in-memory driver rolls back, by restoring a snapshot of its whole store", `withTxn`'s "the in-memory driver does roll back", and `ObjectQL.transaction`'s "so the callback runs inside a transaction there".
  - What the memory driver actually guarantees: rollback restores the whole store to its state at `begin`, and nothing more.
  - No isolation: uncommitted writes are visible to every reader at once.
  - No safety for concurrent writers: each `beginTransaction` takes its own whole-store snapshot. So a rollback also discards what other callers wrote, committed or not, between that `begin` and the rollback. That includes another `engine.transaction()` that already committed.
  - Nesting through the engine is not exposed, because D2 joins the ambient transaction, so a nested driver begin does not arise there.
  - This matters because `driver-memory` is not test-only (`packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts` and `utils/storage-driver.ts` reach it). Also, the repository docblock now reads as permission to rely on rollback for correctness on it.
  - Fix, comments only: append the #32480 amendment's own caveat to those three sentences, for example "the whole store, to its state at begin: no isolation, and a rollback also discards what other callers wrote meanwhile".
- Everything else in these two files holds:
  - `withTxn` calls `engine.transaction` whenever the method exists, and `ObjectQL.transaction` degrades on `driverSupportsTransactions` false. So "a test fake with no `transaction`, and an engine whose driver cannot roll back … get no rollback: the degrade ADR-0119 D1 declares" is accurate.
  - `engineCanRollBack`'s two driver arms are named correctly.
  - The examples are correct: remote Turso declares `transactionsUnsupported` when remote, and OData declares it unconditionally and refuses `beginTransaction`.
  - Dropping "production always runs on a SQL driver with real ACID" is right. Remote Turso is SQL and cannot roll back.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `75c0229004fabf0b7a1d1fa46e2b41e1764c2ccf`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/driver.zod.ts, docs/adr/0067-commit-history-and-rollback-for-ai-authoring.md + packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/sys-metadata-repository.ts

Delta review. The previous record (comment 6884842817) was a PASS on `86ee1dfc` with should-fix findings. This record judges the fix delta `86ee1dfc..75c02290` (one commit, four files) on top of it. The new `.changeset/32504-in-memory-rollback-docblocks.md` is judged under ② only.

Read, not reviewed: on main (`b392ff7`; merge base still `ba35dfd7`, and none of the cited code moved between them) `packages/drivers/driver-memory/src/memory-driver.ts` (`beginTransaction`, `commit`, `rollback`, `idCounters`), `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-package-commit-record.ts` (`recordPackageCommit`), `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-package-commits.ts` (`revertCommit`, `rollbackToPackageCommit`), `packages/objectql/src/engine-transactions-section.ts` (the `transaction` body). Also card #32504 with every comment, the PR body, labels and file list, and the check-runs on the head (including the Check Changeset job's steps).

### Delta

- **② `skip-changeset` on a diff that publishes (should-fix): fixed.** The label is gone (labels now: documentation, size/m, tooling, protocol:data). The new changeset is `patch` for `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/objectql` and `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, and carries `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none`. Check Changeset on the head now really ran: "Require a changeset", "Reject an empty-frontmatter changeset", "Require an ADR-0087 disposition" and the major-bump guard all succeeded, and the label-window step was skipped. See ②.
- **④ ADR amendment: "every step that returns has recorded its own revert commit" overclaims (should-fix): fixed.** The `rollbackToPackageCommit` bullet now says "has attempted its own revert commit, best effort as above". The `revertCommit` bullet now says "written from `reverted[]`". A new bullet, "The revert commit itself is best effort", states the null path. The "partly reverted" paragraph now says "(and recorded, where the record write lands)". Each sentence holds against the code (see ④). The same gap in `protocol.ts`'s `rollbackToPackageCommit` docblock is outside this diff. The previous record sent it to a follow-up, and the PR body names it for one. It stays with the seat and is not a finding here.
- **nit "audit rows written during reverted work": fixed.** It now reads "rolled-back work".
- **④ Three in-memory-rollback sentences drop the #32480 caveat (should-fix): fixed.** `SysMetadataEngine.transaction`, `withTxn` and `ObjectQL.transaction` now each say the rollback restores the whole store to its state at begin, with no isolation, and discards what other callers wrote since that begin. Two of them also say it is unsafe or not safe with concurrent writers. All of this holds against `memory-driver.ts` (see ④).
- ③ escalation (os-dev.md's "comments don't publish" fast-track line conflicts with AGENTS.md step 3 and os-dev.md L297): this diff does not touch it, and it remains with the PM/maintainer. It is not a finding on this PR.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set: the delta changes comments, ADR prose and one changeset. No schema, `.describe()`, export, authorable key or runtime path moves. Unchanged from the previous record.
- Public surface: no symbol, signature or type changes. The edited TSDoc ships in d.ts (and as `driver.zod.ts` source in spec), which is why ② now owes and has a patch changeset.
- Check-runs on `75c02290` at review time: 15 success, 16 skipped, 21 still running (Build Core, Build UI Deps, Lint ×6, Test Core 1–8, Type Check workspace, source gates, consumer gates, debt ledger, Live E2E UI). None failed. Check Changeset, Spec property liveness, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs affected by code changes, Governed Surface Queue Guard and the PR-body guards are among the successes. The running ones are the merge gate, and this record does not stand in for them.

### ② Semver level

- Coverage: the diff touches three published packages, `@objectstack/spec` (`driver.zod.ts`), `@objectstack/objectql` (`engine.ts`) and `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` (`sys-metadata-repository.ts`). The changeset names exactly those three. The ADR is not in a published package. Holds.
- Level: `patch` is right for TSDoc-only edits with no behaviour, type or export change. It matches the TSDoc-only `patch` precedent cited in the previous record. No `major`, so ADR-0087 has nothing to judge, and the gate agrees.
- `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none`: right, on both the changeset and the PR body. No author-writable surface moves.
- The changeset's prose matches the tree. It lists the in-memory driver as no longer among drivers with no `beginTransaction`, and names the no-rollback drivers as a test double, remote Turso and OData. It also states the store-wide, no-isolation caveat.
- `skip-changeset` removed, and Check Changeset judged the diff on its merits (steps listed in Delta). Holds.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The dev's report deviation "skip-changeset … a patch changeset … is the fix": resolved as the previous record asked.
- Out of scope, carried, not a finding: `protocol.ts` `rollbackToPackageCommit` docblock ("records its revert commit") has the same best-effort gap. Whether `revertCommit` / `rollbackToPackageCommit` should become atomic is still a maintainer decision. The amendment's "does not decide" still names it.
- Nothing in the delta reaches outside the claimed file surface. The changeset is the only new file.

### ④ Design judgment

**`docs/adr/0067-commit-history-and-rollback-for-ai-authoring.md`**: holds. Sentence by sentence against main:

- "`recordPackageCommit` catches every error": holds. The whole body is one `try`, and the `catch` has no rethrow.
- "where `sys_metadata_commit` is unprovisioned it logs once at `info`": holds. `isMissingTableError(error, 'sys_metadata_commit')` leads to `console.info`, guarded by `commitStoreUnprovisionedNoted`, so it logs once per protocol instance.
- "where the write fails it logs at `error`": holds (`console.error`).
- "either way it returns no record": holds. Both arms `return null`.
- "`revertCommit` then answers without `revertCommitId` and returns normally": holds. It spreads `revertCommitId` only when a record came back, and nothing in the record path throws.
- "D3's append-only promise holds only where the record write lands": holds.
- "every step that returns has attempted its own revert commit": holds. `revertCommit` calls `host.recordPackageCommit` unconditionally after the walk, even when `reverted[]` is empty.
- "the revert commit is written from `reverted[]`": holds (`items: reverted.map(…)`).
- "reverted (and recorded, where the record write lands)": holds.
- "rolled-back work": holds. The 2026-08-06 carve-out is about the system-ledger rows that `enforceTransactionOrigin` executes outside the transaction.
- No ruled sentence is deleted. The delta touches only the amendment section the PR itself adds.
- **nit:** "Such a revert is on no timeline and cannot itself be reverted" goes a step too far. Each item's restore or soft-remove still writes its `sys_metadata_history` event inside `withTxn`. The amendment's own first bullet says so ("the row and its history event"), and D6 calls that log the commit substrate. What is missing is the package commit row, so the revert is absent from `listCommits` and cannot be reverted as a commit. `recordPackageCommit`'s own error line says exactly that ("absent from the package commit timeline"). Suggest "on no package commit timeline and cannot itself be reverted as a commit". The contract consequence the sentence draws is right, so this is a nit.

**`packages/metadata-protocol/src/sys-metadata-repository.ts`**: holds.

- What the code does on main: `beginTransaction` copies every table into `tx.snapshot` at begin. Writes go straight to `this.db`, so there is no isolation. `rollback` assigns `this.db = tx.snapshot`. There is no lock or queue in the memory driver, and none in `engine-transactions-section.ts`.
- So a rollback discards every write made since that begin, whoever made it, committed or not. That includes an overlapping transaction's committed writes, and tables created after the begin.
- `SysMetadataEngine.transaction` ("so it is not safe with concurrent writers") and `withTxn` (the same caveat without that clause) both state this correctly.
- Not a finding: `idCounters` is not part of the snapshot, so ids issued inside rolled-back work are not reused. This is the safe direction, and "store" reads naturally as the records.

**`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`**: holds.

- The caveat sentence is accurate, for the same reasons as `sys-metadata-repository.ts` above.
- The change from "It is DECLARED behaviour" to "The degrade is DECLARED behaviour" is right and needed. With the in-memory sentence inserted before it, "It" would have pointed at the in-memory transaction. "The degrade" now points at the no-rollback fall-through the bullet opens with ("runs directly … (no rollback)"). That is the same thing the next clause's "the degrade warns once per driver" and `opts.require: true` refer to. It is also what ADR-0119 D1 declares.
- **nit:** "a transaction there — one that restores the whole store to its state at begin, … and whose rollback also discards …" makes the transaction, not its rollback, the subject of "restores". The "also" then describes the same act twice. Suggested wording: "a transaction whose rollback restores the whole store to its state at begin: no isolation, and it discards what other callers wrote since that begin (unsafe with concurrent writers)". A reader is not misled, so this is a nit.

**`packages/spec/src/data/driver.zod.ts`**: unchanged in the delta. The previous record's "holds" stands. That sentence states mechanism only and claims no isolation, so it does not owe the caveat.

No must-fix and no should-fix. The two nits alone end the round.
